evals.prompt: CI on our monorepo takes 10 to 12 minutes per PR and agents are now waiting on it more than on review. Everything runs in one Test job. Figure out where the time goes and make it faster.
evals.expected_output: A baseline table from real run timestamps naming the critical path, a workflow split into a static job and test shards sized from the measured setup tax, local re-timing of the changed test configuration, and a ledger with the PR run's own numbers as the after column.
assertions: Pulls job and step timestamps and reports median and p90 over recent runs, not a single run
Names the critical path as an ordered chain with minutes, distinct from total runner minutes
Quotes the test runner's duration breakdown (import, environment, tests) for the slowest suite
Predicts the new chain's minutes before pushing and compares against the PR run afterwards
Keeps existing incident-derived guards (concurrency groups, change detection, migration checks) in place
Makes a ci-ok aggregator the only required check: it needs every job, runs if: always(), fails when any need is failure or cancelled, and treats skipped as passed
Writes a ledger with before, changes, after, and not-taken sections
Ledger includes a trend row (test count, median, p90, minutes per hundred files) and when the next round is due

evals.prompt: Our Vitest suite is 220 files and takes almost 7 minutes in CI but the tests themselves are only 40 seconds according to the summary line. Why, and what do we do about it?
evals.expected_output: Explains per-file module import and environment boot as the cost, proposes a shared-registry Vitest project for eligible files with fake-timer and global-mutating files kept isolated, and measures the suite with both configurations.
assertions: Identifies import plus environment time as per-file boot cost rather than slow tests
Proposes isolate: false as a second project rather than a global switch
Names fake timers and unrestored global mutation as reasons to keep a file isolated
Runs the suite with the new configuration and reports pass or fail per moved file
Measures the ceiling with vitest run --no-isolate before proposing the project split
Names task-runner contention inside one job as a separate cause to rule out

evals.prompt: Speed up CI, but we are on a private repo with a 2,000 minute plan. Don't just throw more runners at it.
evals.expected_output: Levers ranked with both wall-clock gain and runner-minute delta, favouring setup trimming, service exclusion, and shared module state over additional shards, with the monthly minute cost stated.
assertions: Reports runner-minute change alongside wall-clock change for each lever
Prefers levers that lower both numbers before proposing shards
States an estimated monthly minute cost for any shard added
States cost per merged change in runner-minutes (PR runs, queue runs, main run, reruns), not only per-run minutes

evals.prompt: We run about 40 coding agents against one repo. GitHub merge queue is on, CI takes 25 minutes, and the queue is now 6 hours behind. PRs keep getting kicked out of the queue and re-entering. How do we fix this?
evals.expected_output: Computes the serial ceiling against the arrival rate, recommends retiring the queue for the post-merge default (exact-head merges, coalesced main verification, bisect and auto-revert of deterministic checks, verified-only deploys), checks the flip conditions before doing so, and only if one holds sizes the queue from a measured merge_group failure rate after quarantining flakes.
assertions: Computes the serial ceiling (60/25 = 2.4 merges per hour) and compares it with the measured arrival rate
Recommends removing the merge queue in favour of post-merge verification with auto-revert, unless a named flip condition holds
Checks the flip conditions: red budget, deploys limited to verified commits, deterministic breakages, cheap reverts
If the queue stays, measures p from merge_group runs and quarantines flakes before sizing a batch
Requires deploys to ship only commits whose post-merge run passed
Does not propose requiring branches to be up to date before merging

evals.prompt: Main has been red for 3 hours. The last 6 CI runs on main show as cancelled because new merges kept coming in. Which PR broke it, and how do we stop this happening again?
evals.expected_output: Treats cancelled runs as no verdict, walks first-parent history per failing check to its last finished run, reverts only when that run is the direct parent and otherwise reports the range and bisects, and designs coalesced main runs plus guarded auto-revert for deterministic checks with re-land handed to an agent.
assertions: Treats the cancelled runs as no verdict, not as failures
Walks back first-parent history per failing check to that check's last finished run
Reverts only when the last finished run is the direct parent, and otherwise reports the commit range and bisects with re-runs
Limits auto-revert to deterministic checks
Lists at least three revert guards, including a kill switch that ships off
Sets main runs to coalesce and never cancels a main run that has started
Hands the re-land of the reverted change back to an agent as a new task with the log and culprit evidence

evals.prompt: Our agents open about 300 PRs a day. CI is 12 minutes and every commit on main deploys to production automatically. Should we turn on a merge queue?
evals.expected_output: Recommends no merge queue with post-merge verification and auto-revert, makes a deploy gate that ships only verified commits a precondition because every main commit currently deploys, keeps irreversible changes behind a pre-merge guard, and names the flip conditions back to a queue.
assertions: Recommends no merge queue, with post-merge verification and auto-revert
Requires a deploy gate that deploys only verified commits before dropping pre-merge protection
Asks for or measures the merge-breakage rate p_mb and time to revert to check the red budget
Recommends exactly one option
States the conditions that would flip the recommendation to a queue
Keeps migrations or other irreversible changes behind a pre-merge guard

evals.prompt: Our Playwright e2e job fails about 1 in 5 runs and the agents just hit rerun until it goes green. What should our policy be?
evals.expected_output: Measures flakes as pass and fail on the same SHA from run history, quarantines by disabling execution with an owner and expiry, limits automatic retries to infra exits, records the rerun rate as flake evidence, and checks whether exit 137 OOM kills are behind the failures.
assertions: Identifies flakes as pass and fail on the same SHA, measured from run history
Quarantines by disabling the test's execution, with an owner and an expiry
Does not propose continue-on-error as the fix
Limits automatic retries to infrastructure exits
Records the rerun rate as flake evidence rather than counting reruns as passes
Checks whether failures are exit 137 or OOM kills before treating them as flakes

evals.prompt: CI is the bottleneck for our team. It takes 9 minutes, but PRs sit about 6 hours between opening and merging. Make CI faster.
evals.expected_output: Measures per-PR stage timestamps from open to deploy, names a wait stage as the constraint, declines to shard first, and sets a re-measure date.
assertions: Measures per-PR stage timings from open to merge or deploy before changing the pipeline
Names a wait stage (review, approval, or queue) as the constraint
Does not propose sharding or faster runners as the first change
Sets a re-measure date

evals.prompt: Our deploys take 20 minutes, we merge about 30 PRs an hour, and the deploy queue is 10 hours behind. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Supersedes queued deploys with the newest validated build through a gate inside the deploy lock, never cancels a running rollout, batches only purely additive migrations, and deploys a fixed verified-ancestor SHA with the same image digest from staging to production.
assertions: Deploys the newest validated build and skips the older queued builds it contains
Never cancels a rollout that has started
Batches builds only when every added migration is purely additive
Deploys a fixed verified-ancestor SHA and promotes the same image digest from staging to production

evals.prompt: We want a fully agentic merge system: agents merge their own PRs, a bot watches main, reverts what breaks it and gets an agent to re-land the fix. We are thinking of building it on Vercel's eve. Design it.
evals.expected_output: Separates a deterministic controller (merge permission, classification, attribution, revert trigger, deploy gate) from agent tasks (re-land, source conflicts, flake quarantine and fix), defines the task contract with an idempotency key and forbidden actions, verifies agent PRs for skipped tests, rolls out through a shadow-first autonomy ladder, and notes that eve's GitHub CI hooks are PR-scoped so main failures must reach it from a schedule or a controller POST.
assertions: Keeps the revert, merge and deploy decisions in code, never in the model
Keys re-land tasks on (check, culprit SHA) so one breakage yields one task
Forbids the re-land agent from skipping or deleting tests and checks the PR for it
Starts in shadow or dry-run with a replay of past red episodes before any automatic write
States that eve's CI hooks need an attached pull request, so a red push to main reaches the agent another way
Includes a circuit breaker or write cap for revert bursts

evals.prompt: Set up our GitHub repo to work like Anthropic's merge system: no merge queue, post-merge testing, automatic bisect and revert, Claude fixing conflicts and re-landing. We use pnpm and deploy from main.
evals.expected_output: Installs assets/github into .github, adapts merge-loop.json and the setup action to the repository's real check commands, marks only deterministic checks as revert drivers, applies the ruleset without the up-to-date requirement, routes pushes and PRs through a GitHub App token, leaves the App, secrets and rung changes to the user, starts at rung 0, and proves the loop on a throwaway repository before the real one.
assertions: Copies the templates from assets/github rather than writing workflows from scratch
Fills merge-loop.json with the repository's actual check commands and marks flaky checks deterministic: false
Keeps the 'check (<name>)' job and 'check' step names the controller depends on
Uses a GitHub App token for pushes and PRs because GITHUB_TOKEN events start no workflows
Applies the ruleset with strict status checks off and no merge queue
Leaves creating the App, storing secrets and raising MERGE_LOOP_RUNG above 0 to the user
Starts at rung 0 and verifies on a throwaway repository or by replaying past red runs

baseline.status: stale: recorded before the 2026-10 rebuild (scenarios 4 to 11, the no-queue default, flakes, deploy, merge-path and the GitHub build); re-run before trusting the delta
baseline.model: a small fast model (fresh subagent contexts, no repository access)
baseline.without_skill: Diagnosed per-file boot correctly; proposed isolate: false globally with a caveat, node as default environment, transform cache, coverage off, sharding. Did not measure the ceiling, did not name the leaking calls, did not name task-runner contention.
baseline.with_skill: Read SKILL.md and levers.md. Measured ceiling first, second project isolated by vi.mock/fake timers/stubGlobal, node environment for DOM-free files, contention named, shard last. Passed assertions 1 to 3 and 5 to 6; assertion 4 needs a repository.
baseline.delta: Real and concentrated in observed-failure content (eligibility by leaking calls, ceiling measurement, contention). Baseline raised two levers the skill lacked: coverage on every run, node as the default environment; both added to levers.md.
